deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 240v shows the text of a library loan slip as a mirror image. The ink is faint and reversed, so it is almost certainly bleed-through from the written side (the 'previous page', 240r), seen from the back. The reversed text reads: 'Crelle Journal für d. Mathematik Bd. 44. 45. 46. 47 / 1852. 53. 54. 55.' At lower left are the signature lines 'B. Riemann Dr. ph(il). / Privatdocent hier'. A faint mirrored entry in the lower middle is most likely the date, matching 'Juli 19. 55' on the recto. Taken together, this is a borrowing request of 19 July 1855 for volumes 44–47 (1852–55) of Crelle's Journal (Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik), signed by Riemann as Privatdozent at Göttingen. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically. For context only: the following page (241r) begins an unrelated calculus extremum problem, y = sin(α)^2 cos(α)/a^2 with x = cos α, giving y = (x - x^3)/a^2 and dy/dx = (1 - 3x^2)/a^2. This is the classic optimal-lamp-height illumination problem. It is not on this folio.

results.what: Library loan record: Riemann, Privatdozent, borrowing Crelle's Journal vols. 44–47 (1852–1855), apparently dated 19 July 1855

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries only mirror-image bleed-through of a book-loan slip, with no mathematical content. At most it is a minor biographical datum about Riemann's reading in 1855.
transcription_corrections: The writing is mirror-reversed (bleed-through from the recto). It reads 'Crelle Journal für d. Mathematik Bd. 44. 45. 46. 47 / 1852. 53. 54. 55.' and duplicates the recto entry.
The signature lines read 'B. Riemann Dr. ph. / Privatdocent hier'. 'Privatdocent' and 'hier' are fairly secure given the mirrored letter shapes.
The faint mirrored text in the lower middle, transcribed as '[?]', is most plausibly the date '19/7 55' or 'Juli 19. 55', matching the recto.
